title: There's a Waterfall in Antarctica That Runs Blood Red

scenes.text: There's a waterfall in Antarctica that runs blood red.
It pours out of the Taylor Glacier, five stories tall, staining the ice like spilled paint.
Explorers found it in 1911 and blamed red algae. They were wrong for a hundred years.
The water comes from a lake sealed under the ice, so salty it stays liquid below freezing, and loaded with iron.
The moment that iron meets air, it rusts. The waterfall is bleeding rust.
Microbes even live in that pitch black lake. Red waterfall. Rusty answer.

description:
There's a waterfall in Antarctica that runs blood red.
Blood Falls spills from the Taylor Glacier in the McMurdo Dry Valleys. Discovered in 1911 and blamed on red algae, it is actually iron-rich, hypersaline brine from a lake trapped beneath the glacier; the iron rusts the instant it meets air.
Would you drink water that has been sealed under a glacier for ages?
first_comment: Bonus: the lake under the glacier has no light and almost no oxygen, and microbes still live there. Where else would you look for life like that?
